title: Neuroscience-based educational intervention for enhancing academic adaptation, self-efficacy, and mental health in undergraduate students
reason: Randomised delayed-baseline experiment: group comparisons of module knowledge quizzes and of self-report scales (academic experiences, self-efficacy, DASS-21, motivation); no per-student Moodle activity measure enters any analysis.

extraction.design: randomised experimental, longitudinal (early vs delayed baseline groups)
extraction.n_quote: The study involved 124 undergraduates (aged 18–29), divided into control (n = 62) and experimental group (n = 62).
extraction.population: undergraduates aged 18-29 in an online asynchronous neuroscience course, University of São Paulo extension system
extraction.lms_indicators: none analysed (completion used only to define treatment fidelity)
extraction.outcome_or_construct: academic experiences (QVA-r), higher-education self-efficacy, DASS-21, IMMS motivation, knowledge quizzes
extraction.notes: Secondary NOREL (self-report constructs). Completion was used only to define treatment fidelity.
